TEXT: Come closer! I won't bite! You here to buy or here to sell?
Welcome! Are you buying or selling?
What's up! Want to see my wares?
Selling your fish? Or do you want some sweet upgrades?
Come in! Warm yourself by the fire. Now... Are you buying or selling?
Well met, friend! Here to buy or off-load your goods?
Are you here to buy or... have you created an new profile for me to buy?
Selling your goods? Or do you want to peruse my wares?
I hope you are not forgetting to use that profile builder. Anyways, what can I help you with?

As I previously mentioned, you put in a data-fish into the terminal over there and choose the desired data to extract from it. | Remember, this destroys the fish, so pick carefully. | Then, with that data extracted, access the profile builder on the whiteboard. | There, you put together an profile by dragging and dropping the data onto one of the slots. | Try to place the correct data into the correct slot and also to combine data to reference the same person for maximum profit. | Then, build the profile and bring it to me to sell.
See you around, Compadre.
Quit wasting my time.
Keep your wits about ya. | Aah reckon somethin' is hidin' en the clouds.
Hey you! | This area is off-limits! | … | Wait one minute... | You’re that newcomer Old Man told us about…

Yeah. | The Old Man found Concrete Cove first and invites only those he trusts to join it. | He spoke highly of you and told us that you were allowed here. | I’d wager he wants to speak with you right away. | Go on, he’s by the ledge.

Ahoy there! | I see that you made it in one piece. | However, I notice that you’re lacking one piece of crucial fishin' equipment. | Your rod! | I’d check by with “Chops” to see if he has any old rods on hand.

Ah! I forgot you’re new here. | Chops is our local dealer when it comes to gear and sellin' our fish. | His shop is located in that doorway with the fire barrel inside it. | I recommend being quick and firm with your dealings with him as he ain’t the guy to become chummy with if you catch my drift. | Anyhow, go talk to him, can’t do any fishing without a fishing rod.
Still can’t see any fishin' rod in your hands. | Go talk to Chops to get that sorted out.

Well, well, well! A new face! | You can call me Chops. | I am the local dealer here supplying fine data-fishers, like you, with all of the gear they need. | I also buy data-fishes and profiles off you, once you have any. | Speaking of which, I see that you have no fishing rod on your person. | That is one of many problems I can solve, for the right price. | … | As you are new… I’d wager you don’t have much disposable income on ya, so I’ll sell you one of my cheaper offerings. | She might be quite beat-up, but she’ll do the job. | Have a look.
There we are. | I hope she is to your liking. | Now, I ain’t a data-fisher, so you’ll have to go back to the Old Man to learn how to actually fish. | See ya around.

Now that you have your hand on a fishin' rod, it’s time to get down to brass tacks on how to data-fish. | To start, you throw that sucker as far into the cloud as you can. | The further you throw, the better the data-fish you can fish up. | From there, you wait for a data-fish to get caught on yer hook. | Then, it’s you against the fish, with a precision-timed reel to start the tug of war… | You have to move yer fishin' rod against the movements of the data-fish. | Precision and tracking are key to tire out the data-fish, so pay attention to which direction you have to move the rod! | And if you have done everything correctly, then you’ll reel in a datafish! | Or a piece of junk… | Regardless, you then sell your data-fish to Chops for a profit or use them to build a profile. | I assume you don’t have your hands on a profile builder yet, so I’d just focus on selling the fish to chops for now. | Happy data-fishin' and a warm welcome to Concrete Cove.
Just toss the hook as far as you can into the Cloud and start fishin'.

Now look at that! | You got yourself a fish! | Nicely done. | Now, go over to Chops; he'll probably want to buy that fish off you. | Or just continue fishin' and sell data-fish in batches. | Just remember that Chops closes up shop 22:00, so conduct yer business with him before then. | Anyways, feel free to strike up a conversation with me if you're lookin' for more tips.
You really are putting in the work with that rod. | Good on ya. | However, it ain't the quanitity of data-fishes that matters... | It's the quality!

Mhm! | You see, the data on a data-fish by itself is worth something but put them together with relevant data, and then you multiplying it's worth. | But you might ask, how do you combine data? | Well, it's easy! Use my patented profile builder duh! | Since you have been doing the work, I'll fork one over at a reasonable price. | I promise it'll be worth every Cloudbuck you spend on it.

There we are! Installed and ready to be used. | ... | Right, you have no clue how to use that thing. | Ok so, let me give you a quick rundown. | Most data-fishes will contain sensitive information about someone. | The terminal on the profile builder allows you to extract any single piece of data from a data-fish. | However, the process destroys the fish, so pick carefully! | With that piece of information, you can access the whiteboard to build a profile. | You slot in one of those piece of data you extracted and boom, you are actively building a profile on someone. | However, there is an art to this that comes in two forms: | 1. Any specific data can be placed anywhere, but the right data in the right slot increases the value of the profile more. | 2. The more accurate the data is to eachother and to the person you are building a profile on, the more truthful and thus valuable the entire profile becomes. | Once you have filled out the profile to your liking, you print that profile onto a driver and sell that driver to me for a profit! | Now, go out there and create some profiles!
How's yer fishin' going, kid?
Watcha' need?
Aye?
Sorry kid, I ain't got anymore tips for ya. | Come back tomorrow and my mind might be alittle more clearer.
Alrighty then.
Very well.
Keep your wits about ya.

Data-fishin' is time-consumin' work. | Yer' gonna realise the day is over faster than you expected. | However, takin' your time to talk to yer fellow data-fishermen, like me and others, usually mentally slows down the perception of time passin'. | Same goes for readin' the contents of a data-fish, or lookin' at Chops's wares or anything that's not directly data-fishin' or starin' out at the Cloud. | So feel free to take your time interacting with Concrete Cove and her residents. | You might even learn somethin' you didn't realise you needed to know. | ... | Anyhoo! That's all I have to say about that.

Here is one important one: Don't lose yer humanity! | Alright, I'm pullin' yer leg. | But seriously... think about what data yer sellin' | Minimizin' the collateral damage you cause with data sold is important for a variety of reasons. | I ain't gonna list the reasons, but here are two important ones: | First, excessive amounts of data-fishin' cause people to invest in alternatives to the Cloud-based communication or in encryption measures. | Second, ruinin' lives is not good for the soul. | I know yer not truly evil, kid... | So don't make the wrong decisions. | ... | I Hope that helps...

It technically ain't yer business readin' the data-fishes' contents... | However, if ye' do, try to keep note on how many people are mentioned in it, and what is mentioned about 'em. | As Chops probably wants me to tell ye', try to avoid sellin' the fishes raw, and instead, hold onto 'em creating profiles. | It's gonna earn ye' a lot more Cloudbucks, but in return, the more complete a profile you build on someone, the more harmful the data sold will become. | It's a multiplyin' effect ye' see. | An name and an address don't mean much in a vacuum, but together, they become more... | Valuable... | But dangerous. | ... | Be careful, kid, that's all I'm askin'.
